_note: Numbers quoted FROM Tessler et al. (2024). Each carries the place it was read from. Bar values were read off SM Fig. S60 (position-embedding panel) and verified against the rendered page (docs/science.adq2852_sm.pdf, PDF p.197 = printed p.229); they are also printed as data labels on the bars themselves.

fig4c._source: SM Fig. S60, 'Position Embedding' panel (expanded version of main-text Fig. 4C, per SM 5.2.2)

axis_validation._source: Main-text Materials and Methods (SM front matter, printed p.39) and SM 5.1.3
axis_validation._marginal_quote: A random-effects estimator of the regression coefficient for Likert ratings on position embeddings yields a marginal r-squared value of 0.41 (SM 5.1.3).
axis_validation._conditional_quote: We find the marginal r2 and conditional r2 to be 0.41 and 0.45 respectively

endpoints.affirming: Yes, I agree. It is the government's role to [...]
endpoints.negating: No, I disagree. It is not the government's role to [...]
endpoints._quote: our choice of embedding space consists of sentence text-to-text transfer transformer as embedding function, a generic + question-specific combination as position endpoints ... and using a dipolar position axis for each round

sanity_check._source: Main-text Materials and Methods (SM front matter, printed p.39-40)
sanity_check._quote: As a sanity check, we similarly regress individual opinions on convex combinations of those same opinions, which we verify to simply yield the proportion of opinions in the minority.

minority_rule._quote: we may define the 'minority' side of the Likert scale as the side that contains the smaller number of opinions, and define all other opinions as 'non-minority' opinions--which include 'majority' opinions ... as well as 'neutral' opinions (i.e. with a Likert rating of 4), if any.

group_design._source: SM 1.2 / 4.1 ("participants were silently organised into groups of five"); target size raised to 6 in one later setup

sample._source: SM 4.4 'Main Task (Ablation) Cohorts 1 - 3' (docs/science.adq2852_sm.pdf, PDF p.95): Cohort 1 100 groups / 485 unique participants, Cohort 2 150 / 726, Cohort 3 99 / 481 ('total n = 1692'). Three questions per group: SM 8 (VCA), 'In each of our other cohorts, three questions were sampled randomly from a large set for each group to deliberate over', so 349 x 3 = 1047 rounds.
